entry.title: OLED iPad Mini, M6 iMac, and New MacBook Pros Available From Today
entry.content:
From today, Apple's new iPad mini with an OLED display, M6 iMac, and its latest MacBook Pro models are available to buy from Apple's online store and in the Apple Store app, with the first pre-orders also arriving to customers today and both devices reaching Apple Store locations and Apple Authorized Resellers.


OLED iPad Mini


The eighth-generation iPad mini is Apple's smallest tablet with an OLED display. The 8.5-inch Super Retina XDR display offers up to 1,200 nits of peak brightness, a 2,000,000:1 contrast ratio, and a 1-nit minimum brightness, with a nano-texture glass option on 256GB and 512GB models for the first time.

The device is powered by Apple's A20 Pro chip and the N1 wireless chip, enabling Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6. At 5.4mm thin and 255 grams, it's the lightest iPad Apple has made. It's also the first iPad with an IP67 water and dust resistance rating, aided by a new Acoustic Display that produces sound through the screen itself, so there are no speaker holes in the enclosure.

A 12MP Center Stage front camera is now located on the landscape side for video calls, and the device supports Apple Pencil Pro and Apple Pencil (USB-C). The display is limited to a 60Hz refresh rate with no ProMotion, which has been the main point of criticism in early reviews.

In the United States, the new iPad mini starts at $699 for the 128GB Wi-Fi model. The 256GB and 512GB configurations are priced at $799 and $999, with nano-texture glass adding $100 on those models, while Wi-Fi + Cellular models start at $849. Education pricing starts at $649.

M6 iMac



Meanwhile, the new iMac is the first update to Apple's all-in-one since the M4 model. The M6 chip brings up to a 12-core CPU and 12-core GPU, with Apple claiming up to 2x faster graphics than the previous generation, alongside Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6, and an optional 2.5 Gigabit Ethernet port on the power adapter.

The iMac with M6 starts at $1,499 for the model with a 10-core CPU and 10-core GPU, while the version with a 12-core CPU and 12-core GPU starts at $1,699. Education pricing starts at $1,449.

Latest MacBook Pro Models



Also launching today are the new MacBook Pro models. The 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 starts at $1,999 and features a 12-core CPU and 12-core GPU, alongside Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6 via Apple's N1 wireless chip.

The new 14-inch and 16-inch MacBook Pro models with touchscreen PROLED XDR displays are also available, starting at $2,899 and $3,399, respectively. Powered by M5 Pro or M5 Max chips, the touchscreen models replace the notch with a Dynamic Island and offer up to 2,000 nits of peak brightness for both SDR and HDR content.

Apple's online checkout system indicates many configurations of the 14-inch and 16-inch touchscreen MacBook Pro models in Space Black and Silver currently ship in 2-3 weeks, so anyone who wants one as soon as possible is likely to have more luck visiting their local Apple Store, where at least some base configurations are typically in stock.

The iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max are tougher than previous generations, but they can still be scratched, chipped or damaged in a drop. A good case also does more than protect your phone: it can improve grip, add a stand or wallet, support MagSafe accessories and give your iPhone a completely different look.

There are thousands of iPhone cases to choose from, ranging from inexpensive silicone shells to rugged cases built for serious drop protection. Price isn’t always a reliable guide to quality, either: a cheap case can split, yellow or develop faulty buttons, while spending more doesn’t necessarily mean you’ll get the best case for your needs.

That’s why we hand-test and compare as many iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max cases as we can. We consider protection, materials, build quality, grip, raised screen and camera edges, MagSafe compatibility, weight, useful extras such as stands and card storage, and how the case feels in everyday use. As pretty as some iPhone cases are, your principal consideration should be protection. Most decent cases offer reasonable protection, but these protective cases have extra robust features while often adding as little bulk as possible by using the latest, strongest materials. Kevlar is the material used to make bulletproof vests—it’s also known as Aramid Fiber—but I wouldn’t try turning a rifle on it. Graphene is even stronger, and would probably make Superman wince trying to snap it in half.

Other protective iPhone cases don’t worry so much about thinness, and bulk up to protect your iPhone from the worst disasters that can befall it. These might suit you if you work in riskier environments or are an active outdoors iPhone user.

Material matters too: Graphene (elastic yet harder than diamond and up to 200x stronger than steel, according to case makers) or Kevlar (the material used to make bulletproof vests) for serious durability. Kevlar is a type of Aramid Fiber, a strong, heat-resistant synthetic material that gives the material incredible strength and stability.

FAQ

1.

What is Apple’s Ceramic Shield protection for iPhones?

Apple introduced Ceramic Shield with the iPhone 12 in 2020, developed jointly with glassmaker Corning, and it’s been standard on every iPhone since (excluding the budget SE line).

It’s made by fusing nano-ceramic crystals into glass, then dipping it in molten salt so potassium ions swap places with smaller sodium ions, creating a compressive surface layer that resists cracking. This gave the original iPhone 12 four times better drop performance than the iPhone 11.

Ceramic Shield 2 arrived with the iPhone 17 lineup in 2025, keeping the same crystal-infusion and ion-exchange process but with a refined composition that’s roughly three times more scratch-resistant than the first generation, while retaining similar drop protection. On the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max, Ceramic Shield 2 protects the front, while the back uses Ceramic Shield.

2.

Why do you need an iPhone case?

Your iPhone is a precision device that lives in an unpredictable world—pockets, bags, countertops, pavement. A case is what stands between an accidental drop and a cracked screen or shattered back. It’s not a small risk either: plenty of new iPhone owners crack a screen within the first ten weeks of ownership (source). The IP68 rating means real dust and water resistance, but that’s a lab result—real life is messier. Add in the daily wear of being pulled in and out of a pocket, plus UV exposure over time, and the damage adds up quietly. A case won’t make your iPhone indestructible, but it absorbs the everyday hits so you don’t end up paying for a repair — or a replacement.

3.

Will the iPhone 18 Pro fit a case for the iPhone 17 Pro?

The iPhone 18 Pro series are virtually identical to the iPhone 17 Pro and Pro Max. Even my iPhone 16 Pro fits in an 18 Pro case, and it works just fine—it looks a bit weird at the back, but otherwise fits nicely. On the other hand, a 17 Pro or 18 Pro wouldn’t fit in a 16 Pro case because of the rear camera positioning. Rokform told Macworld that its iPhone 18 Pro case lineup is compatible with iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 17 Pro models. However, its older iPhone 17 Pro case lineup is not compatible with iPhone 18 models due to camera plateau design differences. Cases designed with tight tolerances might therefore have a problem as the camera plateau on iPhone 18 Pro/Max is about 0.5mm taller than on iPhone 17 Pro/Max.

Leading case manufacturer OtterBox reports that its iPhone 18 Pro/Max cases are “also compatible with iPhone 17 Pro, so the cases can be used interchangeably between those two models”.

New cases are custom-built for each device to guarantee a perfect fit and protection, so buying a case built specifically for your iPhone model is the safest option. Check our roundup of the Best iPhone 17 Cases and Best iPhone 16 Cases for the older models.

4.

Do I need a screen protector if I use a case?

Yes, it’s still worth using a screen protector even if you have a case, as the two provide different but complementary protection. A case protects the back, corners, and edges of your iPhone, while a screen protector is designed to protect the display itself from scratches and cracks.

Tempered-glass screen protectors can help absorb direct impacts and protect against everyday scratches and abrasions. A case with a raised screen lip offers some protection if your iPhone lands face down, but it can’t prevent every object or surface from making direct contact with the screen.

5.

What type of iPhone case offers the best protection?

When it comes to maximum protection for your iPhone, the clear winners are rugged cases built with multi-layer materials and military-grade drop ratings. Rugged cases typically combine a hard polycarbonate outer shell with a shock-absorbing TPU (thermoplastic polyurethane) inner layer, reinforced corners, and raised edges around both the screen and camera to prevent direct surface contact on drops.

While silicone and leather cases offer decent everyday scratch protection, they simply can’t match the impact resistance of a purpose-built rugged case.

When choosing a protective case, look for:

  • Raised screen edge around the front (at least 1mm) to keep the screen safely off surfaces.
  • Raised camera edge (0.5mm minimum, some go up to 3.6mm).
  • MIL-STD-810G certification — a U.S. Department of Defense standard for durability.
  • Reinforced corners for impact absorption.
  • MagSafe compatibility if you wirelessly charge.
6.

Do I need an iPhone case for iPhone 18?

Many consumers damage their devices each year, with cracked, chipped or shattered screens the leading reason for iPhone repairs. A screen protector is an important first line of defense, but a case with a raised screen edge can much better protect the display from everyday knocks and drops, and tough sides and back will reduce the risk of damage from an accidental fall.

Ceramic Shield 2, introduced with the iPhone 17 generation, protects the front of the iPhone 18 Pro and offers three times better scratch resistance than the iPhone 16 Pro. The back uses Ceramic Shield, which Apple says offers four times better crack resistance than the back glass used on earlier models.

The 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max are the best-protected iPhones yet, but a case is still worth buying. It helps keep that pristine finish looking new and, when it’s time to trade up, a well-protected iPhone can retain far more resale value than the cost of the case itself.

How we test iPhone cases

When we receive new cases, we test them for fit, button feel, grip, MagSafe strength and alignment, raised-edge camera and screen protection, bulk, weight, and day-to-day handling. Where we are unable to test a case ourselves, we assess it based on its specifications and our experience with other cases from the same manufacturer that have impressed us. We report manufacturers’ claimed drop-protection metrics. As we have listed iPhone cases only from trusted companies we feel safe in these claims but note that measurement is the maker’s own and not ours or Apple’s.

entry.title: Apple’s M6 MacBook Pro is here: Everything you need to know
entry.content:
Macworld

Apple’s 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 is now available, following its October 27 announcement. Sales begin November 6 through Apple Stores and Apple Authorized Resellers. This model uses the standard M6 chip; it does not introduce M6 Pro or M6 Max versions. Apple also introduced a separate touchscreen MacBook Pro.

The biggest changes center on the processor. M6 moves to a 2-nanometer manufacturing process and increases both CPU and GPU core counts from 10 to 12. It also introduces a dual 16-core Neural Engine and higher maximum memory bandwidth.

Wireless connectivity supplies the other major upgrade: Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6 replace the M5 model’s Wi-Fi 6E and Bluetooth 5.3. Apple claims graphics performance improves by up to 30 percent over M5.

M6 MacBook Pro release date and availability

  • On sale: November 6

Deliveries and sales through Apple Stores and Apple Authorized Resellers begin Friday, November 6, across 35 countries and regions. 

Buy a M6 MacBook Pro at Apple U.S.

Buy a M6 MacBook Pro at Apple U.K.

The U.S. and U.K.  starting price is $1,999/£1,999, or $1,899/£1,899 for eligible education buyers. That matches the outgoing model’s current U.S. starting price, rather than its original launch price. 

We recommend: Apple MacBook Pro (M6, 2026)

Price When Reviewed: $1,999
Best Prices Today: $1999 at Apple

M6 MacBook Pro design: What does it look like?

John Brandon

As expected, the new model continues the familiar aluminum design in Space Black and Silver.

The M6 MacBook Pro retains the same dimensions and weight as its M5 predecessor. It measures 12.31 inches wide, 8.71 inches deep, and 0.61 inch thick (31.26 × 22.12 × 1.55cm), and weighs 3.4 pounds (1.55kg).

As with the predecessor, its controls include a backlit Magic Keyboard, full-height function keys, Touch ID, and a Force Touch trackpad.

M6 MacBook Pro display: Resolution and screen quality

Foundry

Apple has not announced a screen upgrade in this release. The M6 MacBook Pro continues to feature a Liquid Retina XDR display with an optional nano-texture finish and the same display specifications.

  • 14.2-inch mini-LED Liquid Retina XDR display
  • 3024 × 1964 resolution
  • ProMotion adaptive refresh rates up to 120Hz
  • 1,600 nits peak HDR brightness
  • 1,000 nits sustained full-screen HDR brightness
  • Up to 1,000 nits SDR brightness outdoors
  • P3 wide color and True Tone

M6 MacBook Pro processor: What does M6 change?

The M6 uses a 2nm manufacturing process, increasing transistor density, and features a 12-core CPU comprising two super cores, four performance cores, and six efficiency cores. That’s up from the M5’s 10-core CPU. Apple’s Mac mini M6 announcement claimed up to 20 percent faster multithreaded performance than M5, although that testing used a Mac mini. Read more about the M6 in our M6 deep dive.

Graphics also get a boost, with a 12-core GPU replacing the M5’s 10-core version. Neural Accelerators and hardware-accelerated ray tracing return, while memory bandwidth increases from 153GB/s to up to 170GB/s, allowing data to move more quickly between the chip and unified memory.

The M6 introduces a dual 16-core Neural Engine, compared with the M5’s single 16-core engine. For this laptop, Apple reports up to 1.9 times faster Neural Engine performance and 25 percent faster on-device AI workloads versus M5. These are separate measures of performance, with the benefits depending on the task and how an app uses the chip.

The Media Engine retains the M5’s listed capabilities, including hardware acceleration for H.264, HEVC, ProRes, and ProRes RAW, alongside AV1 decoding. Dedicated video encoding and decoding hardware helps handle demanding media tasks efficiently, but Apple’s comparison sheet lists no new codec support for M6.

M6 MacBook Pro RAM: How much memory does it have?

The M6 MacBook Pro starts with 16GB of unified memory, with 24GB and 32GB configurations also available – the same capacities offered with M5. However, memory bandwidth increases from 153GB/s to up to 170GB/s, helping the chip access data more quickly.

Additional unified memory gives applications and graphics workloads more room to operate simultaneously. For local AI, capacity affects which models fit in memory, while bandwidth affects how quickly data can move.

Buying advice: Choose 16GB for everyday productivity; consider 24GB for heavier multitasking and creative work, or 32GB for memory-intensive projects and local AI experimentation.

M6 MacBook Pro Connectivity: What ports and wireless options are there?

Wireless connectivity improves with Wi-Fi 7 (802.11be) and Bluetooth 6, replacing the M5 model’s Wi-Fi 6E and Bluetooth 5.3. Wi-Fi 7 availability varies by country.

The physical connections remain unchanged, including three Thunderbolt 4 (USB-C) ports, HDMI, an SDXC card slot, and a 3.5mm headphone jack with support for high-impedance headphones.

M6 MacBook Pro battery, MagSafe, and charging

Apple rates the M6 MacBook Pro for up to 24 hours of video streaming or 16 hours of wireless web browsing, matching the M5 model. These are Apple’s test figures; we’ll be running our own independent battery tests to establish whether M6 delivers better endurance during everyday work or more demanding tasks.

In the U.S. a 70W USB-C power adapter ships with both models, this is an extra expense in the U.K. and Europe (as was the case for the M5 model). Fast charging requires a 96W or higher USB Power Delivery source, so buyers who want that capability should check their adapter’s output. The listed 70W adapter does not meet Apple’s fast-charging requirement.

Should you buy the M6 MacBook Pro?

Buy if: You need a replacement now and the standard MacBook Pro meets your workload. Buyers moving from older machines are more likely to notice the improvement than recent M5 owners.

Don’t buy if: Your M5 already handles your work comfortably. Wait for independent benchmarks before paying to replace it, especially if one particular application drives your decision.

Which configuration? Prioritize memory around the projects you actually run. For demanding graphics, large datasets, or professional video work, compare the full specifications and benchmarks of Pro and Max models rather than choosing solely by the newer “M6” name.

Wait if: The M6 Pro and M6 Max are rumoured to launch in 2027, if you need the extra power wait for that.

When does Apple update the MacBook?

Of the five generations of MacBook Pro, five have been released in the October/November timeframe. The list below also demonstrates that Apple doesn’t always introduce the standard, Pro and Max versions of a chip generation together.

  • M5 Pro & M5 Max MacBook Pro: March 2026
  • M5 MacBook Pro: October 2025
  • M4, M4 Pro & M4 Max MacBook Pro: November 2024
  • M3, M3 Pro & M3 Max MacBook Pro: November 2023
  • M2 Pro & M2 Max MacBook Pro: January 2023
  • M2 MacBook Pro: June 2022
  • M1 Pro & M1 Max MacBook Pro: October 2021
  • M1 MacBook Pro: November 2020

entry.title: Should you buy a MacBook Pro now? M6, touchscreen and older models compared
entry.content:
Macworld

Apple’s M6 MacBook Pro and new touchscreen MacBook Pro models with M5 Pro and M5 Max chips are all on sale now, joining the existing non-touch M5 Pro and M5 Max range. If you’re buying your first MacBook Pro or replacing an older laptop, there’s plenty to choose from. If your M4 or M5 MacBook Pro still meets your needs, an upgrade is harder to justify unless you particularly want the touchscreen model’s OLED display and lighter design.

The MacBook Pro is best suited to creative professionals, developers, engineers and others who need sustained performance, a premium display, extra ports or large amounts of memory. For web browsing, office work, studying and light creative tasks, the MacBook Air is likely to offer better value.

Price matters, too. Following Apple’s $300 to $500 MacBook Pro price increases in June 2026, discounted and refurbished models remain worth considering. Compare the new arrivals with non-touch M5 Pro and M5 Max deals and remaining entry-level M5 stock. If your purchase isn’t urgent, waiting for Black Friday offers later in November could save you money.

This guide will help you decide whether to buy now or wait, choose the right MacBook Pro and compare current deals. We’ll also explain when an older or refurbished model makes sense, and whether you’d be better off with a MacBook Air.

Should you buy a MacBook Pro now?

The M6 MacBook Pro and touchscreen MacBook Pro went on sale on November 6, 2026. If you need a replacement now, you can choose between the M6, non-touch M5 Pro and M5 Max models, and the premium PROLED XDR touchscreen range. However, we recommend waiting for Black Friday for the best prices, although the newest MacBooks are unlikely to see significant discounts.

Buy a MacBook Pro now if:

  • You’re upgrading from an Intel Mac: Apple is ending support for Intel Macs, so if you haven’t yet switched to Apple Silicon, now is a good time to do so. As Intel Macs reach the end of support, they’ll stop receiving security updates, leaving them vulnerable to newly discovered security flaws.
  • You need a new laptop: If your current Mac is broken, unreliable or slowing you down, there’s little reason to wait.
  • You edit video or create content: Whether you’re editing 4K video, working in Photoshop or Lightroom, producing music or creating 3D graphics, the MacBook Pro delivers the sustained performance creative professionals need.
  • You’re a software developer, engineer or AI professional: Compiling code, running virtual machines, working with AI models or processing large datasets is much faster on the MacBook Pro, particularly the M5 Pro and M5 Max models.
  • You need sustained performance: Unlike the fanless MacBook Air, the MacBook Pro uses active cooling to maintain peak performance during long exports, renders and other demanding workloads.
  • You need professional features: The MacBook Pro offers a Liquid Retina XDR or PROLED XDR display with ProMotion, HDMI, an SDXC card slot, MagSafe charging and higher memory and storage options than the MacBook Air.
  • You find an excellent deal: A discounted MacBook Pro can be a good buy if it meets your needs. Compare its memory, storage, display and processor with the new models before deciding whether the saving is worthwhile.

When shouldn’t you buy a MacBook Pro?

The MacBook Pro is an excellent laptop, but it isn’t the right choice for everyone. If you don’t need its extra performance or professional features, you’ll save money – and probably be just as happy – with a MacBook Air. There are also a few situations where it’s worth waiting rather than buying today.

Don’t buy a MacBook Pro now if:

  • You want a processor upgrade over M5 Pro or M5 Max: The touchscreen models retain the same chip options as their non-touch equivalents. The M6 Pro or M6 Max aren’t expected until 2027.
  • You’re looking for the best price: With new MacBook Pro M6 models now here, discounts on the discontinued MacBook Pro M5 could be more attractive. Black Friday may bring further savings.
  • You mainly use your laptop for everyday tasks: If your workload consists of web browsing, Microsoft Office, streaming, email, video calls or light photo editing, a MacBook Air offers excellent performance for much less money.
  • You’re a student with basic computing needs: If your coursework mainly involves writing essays, researching online or creating presentations, a MacBook Air is likely to be the better value.
  • Portability is your priority: The MacBook Air is thinner, lighter and completely silent thanks to its fanless design, although the touchscreen MacBook Pro is lighter than its non-touchscreen counterpart.
  • You’re on a budget: The MacBook Air delivers outstanding performance for most users while costing significantly less than the MacBook Pro.

For most people, the MacBook Air is the better buy. The MacBook Pro only comes into its own if you regularly run demanding professional workloads that benefit from its active cooling, more powerful chips, superior display, additional ports and higher memory options.

Should I buy a MacBook Pro: At a glance

MacBook Pro: Current line up

Apple’s MacBook Pro range now offers three main choices: the entry-level 14-inch M6, the non-touchscreen M5 Pro and M5 Max models, and the new M5 Pro and M5 Max models with PROLED XDR touchscreen displays. Retailers may also have remaining stock of the previous entry-level M5 MacBook Pro.

MacBook Pro M6

Introduced in October 2026, the 14-inch M6 is the entry-level MacBook Pro. It starts with a 12-core CPU, 12-core GPU, 16GB of unified memory and 1TB of storage. It retains the previous model’s design and non-touch Liquid Retina XDR display, while adding the M6 processor, Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6. Choose it if you want the Pro’s display, ports and active cooling without paying for an M5 Pro or M5 Max configuration. From $1,999/£1,999.

Launched in March 2026, these models introduced Apple’s Fusion Architecture, combining two 3nm dies into a single system-on-chip. They offer:

  • M5 Pro: up to 18-core CPU (6 super cores, 12 performance cores).
  • M5 Max: up to 40-core GPU, up to 128GB RAM, and up to 8TB storage.
  • Thunderbolt 5, Wi-Fi 7, and Bluetooth 6 via Apple’s N1 wireless chip.

Is the touchscreen MacBook Pro worth $400/£400 more?

The touchscreen MacBook Pro’s premium pays for its OLED display, touch input and lighter design. It’s easiest to justify if you spend much of your working day using the built-in screen.

Pros

  • Better display: The tandem OLED PROLED XDR screen offers higher contrast and Adobe RGB support alongside P3, which may benefit photographers, video editors and designers.
  • Touch input: Tap, scroll and pinch to zoom alongside using the keyboard and trackpad, with controls adapted for fingers.
  • Thinner, lighter design: The 14-inch model is about half a pound lighter than its non-touch equivalent. Dynamic Island also replaces the notch.

Cons

  • No processor or rated battery-life upgrade: Equivalent models retain the same M5 Pro or M5 Max chip options and advertised battery-life ratings.
  • Touch won’t benefit every workflow: Its usefulness depends on your apps and preferences. Consider ergonomics, fingerprints and app support before buying.
  • Less value with an external monitor: If you rarely use the built-in display, the non-touch model is likely the better buy.

The $400/£400 difference compares Apple’s starting prices for equivalent configurations. Retailer discounts on non-touch models can widen that gap, so compare matching memory and storage configurations.

What’s the best MacBook Pro price right now?

Foundry

Apple rarely discounts Macs itself. In fact, in June 2026, Apple increased MacBook Pro prices by $300 to $500, making it more important than ever to shop around for a deal.

The price rise came in the middle of Amazon’s Prime Day sale, when the M5 MacBook Pro briefly hit record-low prices. Discounts brought the entry-level model down to $1,499/£1,529, making it one of the best MacBook Pro deals we’ve ever tracked. Prices that low are unlikely to return until a major sales event such as Prime Day or Black Friday.

For the latest prices across all configurations, see our live MacBook Pro deals table below.

When is the best time to buy a MacBook Pro?

Foundry

If you’re looking for the lowest price on a MacBook Pro, the best times to buy are during major sales events such as Amazon Prime Day in June/July or October and Black Friday.

Black Friday is typically the strongest shopping period for MacBook Pro deals, although the lowest prices are often reserved for older or clearance models, and popular configurations can sell out quickly. We expect the Black Friday 2026 deals to start towards the beginning of November.

Another time to look for deals is shortly after Apple launches a new model, as retailers often discount the previous generation to clear remaining stock, making it possible to save hundreds if you don’t need the latest chip.

If you’re a student, you can save all year. Students, teachers, and education staff can typically save $100 to $200 on a new MacBook Pro through Apple’s Education Store. However, the best time to buy is usually during Apple’s annual Back to School promotion in the summer, when qualifying customers can often claim a free pair of AirPods or another bonus gift alongside the education discount. See How to use Apple’s Education Store to get a bargain.

Is buying a refurbished MacBook Pro a good idea?

Foundry

Buying a refurbished MacBook Pro can be a great way to save money – particularly if you buy directly from Apple’s Certified Refurbished Store.

Apple Certified Refurbished Macs are typically around 15% cheaper than brand-new models and come with the same one-year warranty, 90 days of complimentary technical support, and the option to purchase AppleCare+. Every Mac undergoes extensive testing, is cleaned and inspected, and receives genuine Apple replacement parts where necessary.

The main downside is availability. Stock changes daily, so you may need to wait for the exact model, storage capacity, memory configuration, or colour you want. Newer MacBook Pro models also usually don’t appear in the refurbished store until several months after launch.

Third-party retailers, including Amazon, also sell refurbished Macs, but quality standards vary considerably. We generally recommend avoiding Macs that are more than five years old, as they may receive fewer years of macOS and security updates. In some cases, retailers also offer larger discounts on new, previous-generation MacBook Pro models during major sales events, so it’s always worth comparing prices before you buy.

For most buyers, Apple’s Certified Refurbished Store remains the safest and best-value way to buy a refurbished MacBook Pro.

Get the MacBook Pro on Apple’s Refurbished Store.

Which MacBook Pro to choose

Choose the M6 MacBook Pro if you want Pro features such as the better display, extra ports and active cooling, but don’t need the power of the M5 Pro or M5 Max.

Choose the M5 Pro MacBook Pro if you’re a professional who regularly edits 4K video, compiles large software projects, works with RAW photos, produces music or runs multiple demanding applications at once. For most creative professionals and developers, the M5 Pro offers the best balance of performance and price.

Choose the M5 Max MacBook Pro if your work pushes a laptop to its limits. The M5 Max is designed for users editing multiple streams of 8K video, creating complex 3D animations, running large AI or machine learning workloads, or handling visual effects and other GPU-intensive tasks. Unless you regularly perform these types of work, the M5 Pro is likely to offer better value.

Choose an M5 Pro or M5 Max MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display if its OLED touchscreen and lighter design justify the extra $400/£400. Choose between Pro and Max according to your workload; you don’t need the Max chip to get the new display.

What about the MacBook Air?

Stephan Wiesend

If you’re considering a MacBook Pro, it’s also worth looking at the MacBook Air. Apple updated the Air in March 2026, and with a starting price of $1,299/£1,299 (the price increased by $200/£200 in June 2026), it’s significantly cheaper than the MacBook Pro.

The MacBook Air is a good choice if you:

  • Mainly browse the web, use Microsoft Office or stream media.
  • Are a student or home user with light computing needs.
  • Value portability and a silent, fanless design.
  • Want the best value MacBook.

However, the lower price comes with a few compromises. Compared to the MacBook Pro, the Air offers lower sustained performance, a less advanced display, fewer ports, and lower memory and storage limits.

Choose the MacBook Pro if you need:

  • Sustained performance for video editing, coding, 3D rendering or AI workloads.
  • A Liquid Retina XDR display with ProMotion and HDR.
  • A PROLED XDR OLED and touch.
  • More connectivity, including HDMI, an SDXC card slot and additional Thunderbolt ports.
  • Higher-end M5 Pro or M5 Max chips, with up to 128GB of unified memory.

For most everyday users, the MacBook Air is the better value. But if your work regularly pushes your laptop to its limits, the MacBook Pro is well worth the extra investment.

Do you need to upgrade your current Mac?

Apple

Whether you need to upgrade depends on three things: how old your Mac is, whether Apple still supports it, and whether it can keep up with the apps and features you use every day.

If you have an Intel Mac, it’s time to upgrade

With macOS 27 Golden Gate, Apple has ended support for Intel Macs. While Apple is expected to continue providing security updates for the small number of Intel Macs that support macOS 26 Tahoe, that support is likely to last only another year or two.

The only Intel Macs that can run macOS Tahoe are:

  • 16-inch MacBook Pro (2019)
  • 13-inch MacBook Pro (2020, four Thunderbolt ports)
  • 27-inch iMac (2020)
  • Mac Pro (2019)

If your Mac isn’t on this list, it may no longer receive the latest macOS updates and will eventually stop receiving security updates. For more advice, read How long Macs and MacBooks last: Lifespan, support and when to upgrade.

If you’re still using an Intel Mac, we recommend upgrading as soon as your budget allows. Moving from Intel to Apple Silicon is one of the biggest upgrades Apple has ever offered. You’ll benefit from dramatically faster performance, much longer battery life, quieter operation, Apple Intelligence support, and many more years of macOS compatibility. Read our guides to macOS Tahoe and macOS Golden Gate to see what you’ll gain by upgrading.

entry.title: Microscopic teardown reveals secret of iPhone Duo’s surprisingly sharp nano-texture screen
entry.content:
Macworld

The iPhone Duo, which launched last month to mixed reviews, contains a range of technological feats and breakthroughs. One of these is its nano-texture interior screen, which contrasts with the glossy outer screen and helps to conceal the crease that marred so many early (and a fair few more recent) foldable phones.

The Duo has been out for a couple of weeks now, which means the repairs site iFixit has had time to perform its usual thorough teardown. And among other discoveries, the team have shed light on how that screen texture works, and how it bears comparisons to the matt finishes on rival products. Spoiler: it compares very well.

In a post to Twitter/X this week, iFixit discussed this aspect of the teardown. The site used an Evident DSX2000 microscope at increasing magnifications to examine the Duo’s nano-texture screen, along with two other matte surfaces: the screen of an e-ink reader and “a popular matte screen protector film.”

“At low magnification,” iFixit reports, “the difference is clear. The e-ink texture blurs everything underneath. The matt protector softens the pixels. The nanotexture lets far more detail through.”

As the site points out, sharp detail isn’t as much of a priority for an e-ink reader as it is for a smartphone, which may explain why the respective makers would be satisfied with this functional difference. But it doesn’t explain what physical qualities produce the difference. That is explained at higher magnification.

“The nanotexture’s pattern is much smaller and more defined than the protector’s,” the tweet reports, backing this up with photographic evidence. The e-ink reader, by contrast, has a “pillowy texture” which is “huge by comparison.”

The photos are clear. The Duo’s screen features a tight pattern of what look like cells or tiny bubbles, while the screen protector has a swampy, uneven pattern and the e-ink reader features massive polygons.

There’s a real difference here. “Is the iPhone Duo’s nano-texture just a matt screen protector with fancy Apple marketing?” iFixit asks, before concluding: “Verdict: not just marketing.”

What’s even better is that nano-texure layer is easy to replace. If you have AppleCare+, Apple charges just $19 to replace it when it when it gets worn down.

If you’re planning to buy a new iPhone, should you buy now or wait for Black Friday? The iPhone Duo went on sale on October 23, completing Apple’s latest launches, but availability and early reports of inner-display failures complicate the decision for foldable buyers.

Meanwhile, there are some excellent U.K. deals on the discontinued iPhone 17 Pro and Pro Max as retailers clear remaining stock. Apple rarely discounts its newest iPhones directly, and its 2026 price increases have made choosing carefully even more important. Black Friday may bring better offers, particularly through carriers and trade-in promotions, but a strong discount on the right phone can make buying now worthwhile.

In this guide, we explain whether now is a good time to buy each iPhone, which models are worth waiting for, and when to expect the best deals. We’ll help you weigh the appeal of Apple’s newest hardware against the savings available on older models.

When to buy an iPhone in 2026-2027: At a glance

The worst time to buy an iPhone

This is generally in the weeks leading up to Apple’s September launch event, or in the early spring, when new models are expected to be announced. Buying just before a refresh means you could miss out on new features or pay full price for a model that’s about to be superseded.

The best time to buy an iPhone

This depends on where you live:

In the U.K., where most iPhones are sold unlocked and off contract, the biggest savings are typically available during major sales events such as Amazon Prime Day (usually in July and October, and occasionally in March) and Black Friday in late November. However, worthwhile iPhone discounts can be found throughout the year if you know where to look.

In the U.S., where people tend to buy iPhones through a carrier, the best time to upgrade is often during Black Friday when networks enhance their offers with larger trade-in values, bill credits, gift cards, or discounted service plans.

Due to the Black Friday sales, November and December could be a particularly good time to grab a deal on an older iPhone, such as the iPhone 17 Pro or iPhone 17 Pro Max.

Should you buy a new iPhone now or wait?

  • Wait for Black Friday, November 27, 2026.

Ida Blix

September and the months that follow are a much better time to buy an iPhone than earlier in the summer (July and August are usually poor months to buy a Pro iPhone because Apple’s September launch is so close). The iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max and iPhone Duo have now been unveiled, removing that uncertainty.

If you need a phone now, there’s little reason to wait for another annual refresh, and the iPhone 17, 17e and Air are also relatively safe purchases because their successors aren’t expected until spring 2027. See: iPhone 18 and 18e rumors and iPhone Air 2 rumors.

The iPhone 17 remains the strongest value, with a 120Hz ProMotion display, A19 chip, dual 48MP cameras and 256GB of storage for $899/£899 (although it was previously $799/£799). The 18 Pro and Pro Max make more sense if you want the best cameras, performance or battery life, while the Duo is for buyers specifically interested in Apple’s new folding design.

There is, however, one important reason to wait: 2027 could bring a much bigger iPhone redesign. Apple is rumored to be preparing a 20th-anniversary iPhone – the iPhone 19 or 20 with a near-all-screen curved design, under-display Face ID, possible solid-state buttons, a thinner and more efficient OLED display, a larger battery and major camera improvements. That could make 2027 a more significant upgrade year than 2026.

So if your current iPhone is still serving you well, waiting could be worthwhile. If you need a phone now, wait until Black Friday if price is your main concern.

Best iPhone deals right now

If you are based in the U.K. it is possible to buy unlocked iPhones on Amazon – and certain models are frequently discounted. If you can get a good discount it’s always a good time to buy.

Amazon is offering £20 off the iPhone 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max if you are approved for an Amazon Barclaycard.

Should you wait for the iPhone 18?

For most people, there isn’t a strong reason to wait for the iPhone 18. Apple isn’t expected to launch the standard model until spring 2027, so buying an iPhone 17 before the end of 2026 would still give you several months with Apple’s current mainstream model before its replacement arrives.

The iPhone 18 is expected to bring a 2nm A20 chip, potentially 9GB or 12GB of RAM, Apple’s C2 modem and possibly a new 24MP front camera. Extra RAM could prove particularly useful for future Apple Intelligence and Siri features. However, the rear camera system is still expected to consist of two 48MP cameras, while the display may remain broadly similar to the iPhone 17’s 6.3-inch ProMotion panel.

There is also some uncertainty over exactly what the iPhone 18 lineup will look like. A September 2026 rumour suggested Apple could effectively merge the standard iPhone and iPhone Air into a single model, rather than continuing them as two separate devices. If that happens, the iPhone 18 could adopt some of the Air’s thinner, lighter design while retaining the broader appeal of the standard iPhone. For now, though, that remains speculative.

Price is another consideration. With the arrival of the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Duo, Apple increased iPhone prices across the range, so the iPhone 17 now costs $899, $100 more than at launch. When the iPhone 18 arrives, it is likely to inherit that $899 price point, while the iPhone 17 could drop back to around $799 at which you may regret buying it at the higher price.

Wait if you want the newer A20 chip, potentially more RAM, an improved front camera, or are intrigued by the possibility of a thinner redesigned standard model.

Don’t wait if you simply want ProMotion, dual 48MP cameras, excellent battery life and 256GB of storage as standard – the iPhone 17 already delivers all of that.

When does Apple update the iPhone?

Apple typically unveils new iPhones at a dedicated Apple event in September. Preorders usually open the following Friday, with devices shipping and arriving in stores a week later. However, some models arrive later: Apple announced the iPhone 18 Pro, Pro Max and iPhone Duo in September 2026, but the Pro models went on sale September 18, while the Duo followed on October 23.

Apple also launches iPhones earlier in the year, particularly its more affordable models. The iPhone 16e arrived in February 2025 and the iPhone 17e in March 2026. The standard iPhone 18, iPhone 18e and iPhone Air 2 are expected in spring 2027.

These spring launches are often announced via press release, although Apple has also held spring events. Availability typically follows within one to two weeks, but initial supplies can be limited.

Compatible iPhones also receive a major iOS update each year, usually in September, bringing new features that can give an older phone a fresh lease of life.

Read our guide to the next Apple event to find out what’s coming next.

3.

When do iPhone prices drop and by how much?

Based on past experience, Apple is very unlikely to reduce the price of a new iPhone during its first year on sale.

However, when Apple introduces a new generation of iPhones, it usually cuts the price of the previous year’s models. That means September has traditionally been the point when older iPhones become cheaper.

Apple also tends to keep launch prices broadly similar from one generation to the next, at least in the U.S., although exchange rates and other regional factors can affect pricing elsewhere.

In 2024, for example, Apple reduced the price of the iPhone 15 and iPhone 15 Plus by $100/£100 when the iPhone 16 and 16 Plus arrived. The iPhone 16 also fell in price following the launch of the iPhone 17 in 2025. However, because the iPhone 17 doubled the base storage to 256GB, the older iPhone 16 looked less attractive even at $100/£100 less.

In 2026, the pattern changed. Apple actually raised iPhone prices, blaming higher memory costs. Even the year-old iPhone 17 and two-year-old iPhone 16 increased by $100, showing that older iPhones don’t always become cheaper when a new generation arrives.

4.

Is it better to buy from Apple or a carrier?

In the U.S., buying from Apple is usually the better option if you value flexibility. If you pay in full or use Apple’s own financing, the iPhone is unlocked, so you can switch carriers or use another eSIM when traveling. Apple also accepts trade-ins and, importantly, many AT&T, T-Mobile and Verizon promotions are available when buying through Apple.

However, an iPhone bought from Apple but financed through an AT&T, T-Mobile or Verizon device-payment plan is locked to that carrier until it has been paid off. An iPhone bought outright from Apple isn’t.

The main reason to buy directly from AT&T, T-Mobile or Verizon is to take advantage of a particularly good promotion. U.S. carriers frequently advertise large trade-in credits or “free” iPhones, especially when you add a line or switch networks. The catch is that the discount is usually provided as monthly bill credits over 24 or 36 months, so if you leave early you can lose the remaining credits.

In the U.K., Apple sells iPhones unlocked and SIM-free, allowing you to shop separately for a SIM-only plan from EE, Vodafone, O2, Three or an MVNO. This makes it easier to switch networks and can work out cheaper over the life of the phone than bundling the handset and airtime into a single contract.

Apple isn’t necessarily the cheapest place to buy, however. Amazon U.K. and other retailers frequently discount SIM-free iPhones, and there can be substantial savings during sales events such as Black Friday.

Networks can also offer compelling promotions, including enhanced trade-in values, discounted airtime, generous data allowances or lower monthly payments. But make sure you compare the total cost of the contract, rather than focusing on the headline monthly price.

5.

When are the best iPhone deals?

The earliest you could expect to get a discount on the newest iPhones is around Black Friday at the end of November, so you might be planning to hold out until then. However, the deals we tend to see, if any, are usually for older handsets. See our round-up of Best Black Friday iPhone deals for more.

Nor should you expect to get a discount in an Apple Black Friday sale. Apple’s Black Friday sale usually only takes the form of vouchers with select product purchases, rather than a discount, and it is unlikely that the newest iPhone would qualify as in previous year’s new iPhones haven’t been included.

Note that while shopping events like Black Friday get all the attention, that’s not the only time you can get discounts on Apple products: we see discounts all the time. Another event where we see good iPhone deals is Prime Day, which happens in June or July and October every year. So take a look at the iPhone deals for Amazon Prime Day sale to see what you might be able to save.

In our experience, we don’t tend to see discounts on the newest handset until the spring – and these are always from third-party resellers, never from Apple. In fact, we don’t tend to see the iPhone discounted in the U.S. very often, most of the discounts we see are in the U.K. where unlocked iPhones are often sold off-contract at a good discount.

6.

Is it worth buying a refurbished iPhone?

Yes, buying a refurbished iPhone is absolutely worth it for most people, especially if you want to save money without sacrificing quality.

Buying refurbished is a great way to “pick up a bargain” while still getting a premium device. You can typically save 15% to 30% compared to buying new, and sometimes much more on older models.

A common misconception is that refurbished is the same as buying a used phone from a stranger, though. It’s not. A used phone is sold “as-is,” with no guarantee it will work properly. A refurbished phone has been professionally inspected, tested, and repaired if needed, and it comes with a warranty.

If you want the highest quality, Apple’s own refurbished store is the gold standard.

7.

How to check iPhone stock near you

If the iPhone you want has a long delivery estimate, independent stock-checking services can help you find availability elsewhere. Apple Inventory Check lets you search Apple Store stock by country, location, model, color and storage capacity. It covers Apple’s current iPhone range, including the iPhone Duo, iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max, and older models.

Checking nearby stores or choosing a different color or capacity could help you get your phone sooner. Confirm availability through Apple before traveling. For more options, see our guide to iPhone stock-checking services.

Conclusion: When is the best time to buy a new iPhone?

The worst time to buy is usually between July or August, mainly because with new iPhones on the horizon the price of the older handsets are likely to drop very soon.

If you want the newest iPhones then the best deals don’t tend to come before the spring and summer months. If you are happy to buy an older iPhone then you will probably see decent deals around Prime Day and Black Friday – but deals happen all year round. 

We hope this article has proved helpful in reaching an informed buying decision. Remember that good prices can be found all year round, if a retailer is feeling generous and you know where to look: read our guide to the best iPhone deals for more on that.

Wondering how long Apple supports iPhones for? Read How long do iPhones last.

entry.title: Best iPhone 2026: Every iPhone compared
entry.content:
Macworld

Apple’s 2026 iPhone lineup is broader than ever, ranging from the relatively affordable iPhone 17e to the high-end iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max, plus the ultra-thin iPhone Air and the new folding iPhone Duo. That gives buyers more choice, but it also makes picking the right model more complicated than simply choosing the newest or most expensive iPhone.

For most people, the iPhone 17 is the best all-round choice, thanks to its 6.3-inch ProMotion display, strong battery life, dual 48MP cameras and 256GB of storage as standard. The iPhone 17e is the better option if price matters most, while the iPhone 18 Pro is the model to choose for the best cameras and performance. The iPhone 18 Pro Max adds the longest battery life, the iPhone Air prioritises thinness and low weight, and the iPhone Duo offers Apple’s biggest and most flexible display.

Which iPhone is best for you will therefore depend on what you value most. Camera enthusiasts should look closely at the Pro models, heavy users may prefer the Pro Max for its battery life, while parents, older users and anyone trying to keep costs down may find the 17e a much better fit. There can also be excellent value in buying a discounted or refurbished older iPhone rather than paying full price for the latest hardware.

This guide focuses on the best iPhone to buy for different types of user and budget. If you want to dig deeper into the differences between every model see our complete iPhone Buying Guide, where we compare the cameras, displays, performance, storage, battery life and other key specifications across Apple’s current lineup.

Which iPhone to buy: At a glance

1. Apple iPhone 17 – Best iPhone for most people

Pros

  • Excellent overall value
  • ProMotion Always-On display
  • Dual 48MP cameras

Cons

  • No dedicated telephoto
  • Limited to 512GB

Why we recommend it

The iPhone 17 brings several features previously reserved for Pro models to Apple’s mainstream iPhone, including a 120Hz ProMotion display and Always-On support. It also offers the fast A19 chip, dual 48MP cameras, an improved Centre Stage selfie camera, strong battery life and 256GB of storage as standard. For most buyers, it strikes the best balance between price and features.

Buy iPhone 17 if

Buy the iPhone 17 if you want the best all-round iPhone without paying Pro prices. Its 6.3-inch ProMotion display, excellent cameras, strong battery life and 256GB starting storage make it particularly appealing to anyone upgrading from an iPhone 14 or older.

Don’t buy iPhone 17 if

Don’t buy it if you want optical zoom beyond 2x or Apple’s most advanced camera features—in that case, choose the iPhone 18 Pro. The iPhone Air is a better choice if thinness and low weight are your priorities, while existing iPhone 16 owners may find the upgrade relatively modest unless ProMotion and improved battery life are particularly important.

What do you get that you don’t get with the iPhone 17e?

For the extra $200, the iPhone 17 gives you a larger 6.3-inch ProMotion Always-On display, Dynamic Island, a second 48MP Ultra Wide camera with macro photography, a brighter screen, stronger graphics performance, a better 18MP Centre Stage selfie camera and longer battery life. For most people who can afford the difference, it’s money well spent.

What do you get that you don’t get with the iPhone 16?

For $100 more, you get double the base storage at 256GB, a larger 6.3-inch ProMotion Always-On display, an upgraded 48MP Ultra Wide camera, an improved 18MP Centre Stage selfie camera, longer battery life, faster charging and the newer A19 processor. At full price, the iPhone 17 is the better buy.

Key specs

The iPhone 17 combines a 6.3-inch ProMotion display, Always-On support and the A19 chip with dual 48MP rear cameras and 256GB of storage as standard. It offers many of the features most people actually want from a Pro iPhone without the Pro price.

  • Starts at: $899 / £899 (was $799 / £799) for 256GB
  • Display: 6.3-inch OLED ProMotion (120Hz)
  • Chip: A19
  • Storage: 256GB–512GB
  • Cameras: 48MP Main + 48MP Ultra Wide, 18MP front camera
  • Battery: Up to 30 hours of video playback

Should you buy or wait?

Buy now. The iPhone 17 offers excellent value, while the iPhone 18 isn’t expected until spring 2027 and may bring higher prices rather than transformative upgrades. Waiting for Black Friday could make sense if you’re looking for a discount.

Read our full Apple iPhone 17 review

2. Apple iPhone 18 Pro – Best for photography

Pros

  • Excellent triple-camera system
  • Powerful A20 Pro chip
  • Strong battery life

Cons

  • Expensive starting price
  • Overkill for most buyers

Why we recommend it

The iPhone 18 Pro is the model to buy if you want Apple’s best cameras and performance without stepping up to the much larger Pro Max or experimental folding iPhone Duo. Its variable-aperture camera will be a meaningful upgrade for some photographers – although our reviewer found the practical effect modest and valued the manual controls more. The A20 Pro chip, improved cooling, longer battery life and faster charging make it particularly capable for gaming, video and demanding AI workloads. Crucially, it gets the same cameras and processor as the Pro Max, making it the better-value Pro model for most buyers.

Buy iPhone 18 Pro if

Buy the iPhone 18 Pro if you want Apple’s best camera system; need more performance than the standard iPhone offers; regularly play demanding games or use intensive creative or AI apps; or want excellent battery life without carrying the enormous Pro Max. It’s a compelling upgrade for anyone with an iPhone 15 Pro or older.

Don’t buy iPhone 18 Pro if

Most people don’t need the iPhone 18 Pro. The standard iPhone 17 already offers an excellent 6.3-inch 120Hz ProMotion display, A19 chip, dual 48MP cameras, 256GB of storage and strong battery life for considerably less. And if your main priority is screen size and endurance, the Pro Max is the better choice.

What do you get that you don’t get with the iPhone 17?

The biggest advantage is the camera system. The iPhone 18 Pro adds a 48MP Telephoto camera with 4x and 8x optical-quality zoom, plus a variable-aperture 48MP Main camera for improved low-light shooting and greater creative control. You also get the faster A20 Pro chip with a seven-core GPU and improved vapor-chamber cooling for better sustained performance during gaming, video editing and AI tasks.

Key specs

The iPhone 18 Pro combines Apple’s new 2nm A20 Pro processor with a sophisticated triple-48MP camera system, including a variable-aperture Main camera and 4x/8x Telephoto. It retains a manageable 6.3-inch ProMotion display while improving sustained performance, battery life and charging speeds.

  • Starts at: $1,199 / £1,199 (256GB)
  • Display: 6.3-inch OLED ProMotion (120Hz)
  • Chip: A20 Pro, 6-core CPU, 7-core GPU
  • Storage: 256GB–2TB
  • Cameras: 48MP variable-aperture Main + 48MP Ultra Wide + 48MP Telephoto (4x/8x), 18MP front camera
  • Battery: Up to 36 hours of video playback

Should you buy or wait?

The iPhone 18 Pro is available now. Buy it if you want the Pro camera system and performance in a smaller phone – the Pro Max offers the same cameras. Bargain hunters may prefer to hold off until Black Friday on November 27, when retailers and mobile networks may offer trade-in bonuses, contract incentives or modest discounts. Large outright savings are unlikely so soon after launch.

Read our full Apple iPhone 18 Pro review

  • Outstanding battery life
  • Huge 6.9-inch display

Why we recommend it

The iPhone 18 Pro Max is Apple’s ultimate conventional iPhone, combining a huge 6.9-inch ProMotion display with the powerful A20 Pro chip, Apple’s best camera system and the longest battery life in the range. Its biggest advantage over the regular Pro is endurance, with Apple rating it for up to 45 hours of video playback.

Our testing backs up the battery recommendation: the iPhone 18 Pro Max lasted 25 percent longer than the iPhone 17 Pro Max in our Geekbench 4 battery test, with screen brightness fixed at 200 nits. This is a separate measurement from Apple’s video-playback rating and provides another reason to choose the Pro Max if endurance is your priority.

Buy the iPhone 18 Pro Max if

Buy the iPhone 18 Pro Max if you want the largest display on a non-folding iPhone and the longest battery life, regularly use your phone for photography, video, gaming or other demanding tasks, and don’t mind carrying a large and relatively heavy device. It’s particularly well suited to frequent travellers and heavy users who want to minimise charging.

Don’t buy iPhone 18 Pro Max if

Don’t buy it if you prefer a smaller, lighter phone or simply want the Pro cameras and performance. The iPhone 18 Pro offers essentially the same A20 Pro chip, camera system and Pro features in a more manageable 6.3-inch design for $100/£100 less. At 249g, the Pro Max is also particularly heavy.

What do you get that you don’t get with the iPhone 18 Pro?

Not much in terms of features. Both models have the same A20 Pro processor, triple-48MP camera system, variable-aperture Main camera and storage options up to 2TB. The Pro Max instead gives you a larger 6.9-inch display rather than 6.3 inches and substantially better battery life: up to 45 hours of video playback versus 36 hours on the iPhone 18 Pro. You pay an extra $100/£100 for those advantages.

Key specs

The iPhone 18 Pro Max combines Apple’s huge 6.9-inch ProMotion display with the new 2nm A20 Pro chip, three 48MP rear cameras and a variable-aperture Main camera. Its defining advantage is battery life, reaching up to 45 hours of video playback.

  • Starts at: $1,299 / £1,299 (256GB)
  • Display: 6.9-inch Super Retina XDR OLED ProMotion (120Hz)
  • Chip: A20 Pro, 6-core CPU, 7-core GPU
  • Storage: 256GB–2TB
  • Cameras: 48MP variable-aperture Main + 48MP Ultra Wide + 48MP Telephoto, 18MP front camera
  • Battery: Up to 45 hours of video playback

Should you buy or wait?

The iPhone 18 Pro Max is available now. Choose it over the smaller Pro if longer battery life and a larger display justify the extra cost and weight. If your current phone lasts comfortably through the day, there is less urgency to upgrade, and waiting for a discount could make sense. Compare the total cost of carrier offers and trade-ins with buying outright. Bargain hunters may prefer to wait for Black Friday on November 27. Major outright discounts are unlikely so soon after launch, although trade-in offers and contract incentives could be worthwhile.

4. Apple iPhone 17e – Best budget iPhone

Pros

  • Excellent budget value
  • Strong A19 performance
  • 256GB base storage

Cons

  • No ProMotion display
  • No Ultra Wide camera

Why we recommend it

The iPhone 17e is Apple’s most affordable current iPhone, offering modern performance and Apple Intelligence without flagship pricing. It combines the A19 chip with useful upgrades including MagSafe and 256GB of base storage. If you don’t need multiple cameras or a high-refresh-rate display, it delivers the essentials at an attractive price.

Buy the iPhone 17e if

Buy the iPhone 17e if you want a modern iPhone with strong performance and years of software support for as little as possible. It’s particularly appealing to anyone upgrading from an iPhone 12 or 13, switching from Android or buying their first iPhone.

Don’t buy iPhone 17e if

Don’t buy it if you want ProMotion, an Always-On display, Dynamic Island or a versatile camera system. If your budget stretches another $200/£200, the iPhone 17 is a substantially more complete phone.

What do you get that you don’t get with the iPhone 16?

The iPhone 17e gives you the newer A19 chip, longer battery life, 256GB of storage as standard, Apple’s newer C1X modem and Ceramic Shield 2 protection. Its biggest advantage, however, is value: at similar real-world prices, it is generally the smarter long-term purchase.

What don’t you get that you get with the iPhone 17?

The iPhone 17 gives you a larger and significantly more advanced 6.3-inch 120Hz ProMotion display with Dynamic Island and Always-On support, plus a second 48MP Ultra Wide camera. You also get a better 18MP Centre Stage selfie camera, stronger graphics performance and longer battery life. The 17e covers the essentials extremely well, but the iPhone 17 feels much more complete.

Key specs

The iPhone 17e pairs the A19 chip with a 6.1-inch OLED display, 256GB of storage as standard and up to 26 hours of battery life, while omitting premium features such as Dynamic Island, ProMotion and an Ultra Wide camera.

  • Starts at: $699 / £699 (was $599 / £599) for 256GB
  • Display: 6.1-inch Super Retina XDR OLED
  • Chip: A19
  • Storage: 256GB–512GB
  • Cameras: 48MP Fusion Main with 2x optical-quality zoom + 12MP TrueDepth front camera
  • Battery: Up to 26 hours of video playback

Should you buy or wait?

Buy now. The iPhone 17e offers excellent value and isn’t expected to be replaced until early 2027. Discounts could make it even more attractive, but there’s little reason to delay purely for the next generation.

  • Excellent multitasking potential
  • Strong A20 Pro performance

Our verdict

The iPhone Duo’s folding display and side-by-side multitasking offer something no other iPhone can. However, our full review of the iPhone Duo found too many compromises to recommend buying one yet. Optimized apps make good use of the larger screen, but many everyday apps remain awkward or waste the extra space. Camera quality also trails the Pro models. Check your essential apps before considering it.

Buy iPhone Duo if

You specifically want a folding iPhone for reading, watching video or using two apps side by side, and have checked that your essential apps work well on its displays. Try it in person before committing $1,999/£1,999, and check current delivery and collection estimates.

Be prepared to accept uneven app support and battery life that depends heavily on how you use the displays.

Don’t buy iPhone Duo if

You prioritize camera quality, value or established long-term durability. Following reports of cracked inner screens, Apple acknowledged an issue affecting a small number of iPhone Duo units on October 26 and advised affected owners to contact AppleCare for a replacement. The cause and failure rate remain unclear, and Apple has not announced a formal repair program. Our iPhone Duo guide tracks the latest developments.

You should also look elsewhere if you want consistently good app layouts or rely on demanding inner-screen use throughout the day.

Wait for further investigation and longer-term testing if these concerns would make you uncomfortable buying a first-generation folding phone.

What do you get that you don’t get with the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max?

The Duo’s defining advantage is its 7.6-inch folding display, which offers around 50 percent more screen area than the iPhone 18 Pro Max and supports Split View multitasking, while the 5.4-inch outer screen keeps it usable like a compact iPhone when closed. You also get fold-specific features such as Duo Preview, Smart Take, Kid Cue, hands-free video positioning and an under-display inner camera. Apple Pencil (USB-C) support arrived with iOS 27.2 on October 26, adding another way to write, sketch and mark up content on the larger display. The update also introduced Edge Light to illuminate your face during video calls. The trade-off is photography: the Duo has only two 48MP rear cameras, with no dedicated telephoto, variable aperture, ProRes or Apple Log.

Key specs

The iPhone Duo transforms from a compact 5.4-inch phone into a 7.6-inch folding device, providing substantially more room for apps, video and multitasking. It combines two 120Hz ProMotion OLED displays with the A20 Pro chip, dual 48MP cameras, and storage up to 2TB.

  • Displays: 5.4-inch outer + 7.6-inch folding OLED, ProMotion (120Hz)
  • Chip: A20 Pro
  • Storage: 256GB–2TB
  • Cameras: 48MP Main + 48MP Ultra Wide, 12MP outer front camera + under-display inner camera
  • Battery (Apple’s ratings): Up to 44 hours of video playback on outer display; 31 hours on inner display

In our review, battery life depended heavily on which display was used. Intensive gaming or video editing on the inner screen could require charging by mid-afternoon; using the outer screen more often left plenty of charge at bedtime. Our standard battery benchmark app crashed on launch, so we don’t have directly comparable laboratory results.

Should you buy or wait?

We recommend waiting for better app support. If you still want the folding design, try it in person and check your essential apps before buying. See our iPhone Duo guide for the latest on reported display and hinge problems. Our iPhone Duo guide tracks the latest developments.

Buy the iPhone Air if

Buy the iPhone Air if you want a premium large-screen iPhone that feels exceptionally thin and light in the hand. It’s ideal for buyers prepared to sacrifice some camera flexibility and battery life in exchange for a much sleeker design.

Don’t buy iPhone Air if

Don’t buy it if photography or battery life are higher priorities. The iPhone 17 offers a more versatile dual-camera system for less money, while a Pro model is better suited to demanding photographers and power users.

The iPhone Air’s biggest advantage is its exceptionally thin and light titanium design. You also get a slightly larger 6.5-inch display, the more powerful A19 Pro chip and storage options up to 1TB. Those benefits come at the expense of the iPhone 17’s useful 48MP Ultra Wide camera, making the Air primarily a choice for buyers who value design and portability over versatility.

Why we recommend it

The iPhone 16 still delivers fast everyday performance thanks to its A18 chip, supports Apple Intelligence and includes a versatile dual-camera system with an excellent 48MP Main camera. Its main appeal in the current lineup, however, is price: it only makes sense when discounted significantly below the newer models.

Buy iPhone 16 if

Buy the iPhone 16 if you find it heavily discounted and want Apple Intelligence, a capable dual-camera system and features such as Camera Control and the Action button without paying for the latest generation.

Don’t buy iPhone 16 if

Don’t buy it at full price. The iPhone 17e offers newer hardware, twice the base storage and longer battery life for less, while the iPhone 17 is considerably more advanced for only a little more money.

What do you get that you don’t get with the iPhone 17e?

The iPhone 16 has a second 12MP Ultra Wide camera, giving it greater photographic versatility, as well as Camera Control and the Action button. Those features may make it preferable to the 17e for photography-minded buyers, but only if the price is right.

What do you miss compared with the iPhone 17?

The iPhone 17 gives you a larger 6.3-inch ProMotion Always-On display, newer A19 processor, upgraded 48MP Ultra Wide camera, improved 18MP Centre Stage selfie camera, longer battery life and 256GB of storage as standard. Unless the iPhone 16 is heavily discounted, the 17 is easily worth the difference.

Key specs

The iPhone 16 combines the A18 chip with a 48MP Fusion Main camera, 12MP Ultra Wide camera, Camera Control, the Action button and Apple Intelligence support. It remains a capable smartphone, but its 128GB starting storage and older display make it less compelling than the newer iPhone 17e and iPhone 17.

Should you buy or wait?

Don’t buy at full price. Only consider the iPhone 16 if it’s heavily discounted below the iPhone 17e; otherwise, Apple’s newer models offer substantially better value.

Which iPhone has the best camera? iPhone 18 Pro

Apple

The iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max have the best camera systems of any current iPhone. Both models use the same triple-48MP rear camera setup, so there is no photographic advantage to choosing the larger Pro Max unless you also want its bigger display and longer battery life.

The headline upgrade is the 48MP Main camera with variable aperture, which gives photographers more control over depth of field and should improve low-light performance. The Pro models also include a 48MP Ultra Wide camera and a 48MP Telephoto camera with 4x and 8x optical-quality zoom, giving them far more flexibility than Apple’s cheaper iPhones.

The standard iPhone 17 is still an excellent camera phone, with 48MP Main and Ultra Wide cameras, plus an improved 18MP Centre Stage front camera. For everyday photography it will be more than enough for most people, but it lacks the dedicated telephoto lens, longer zoom and advanced video features of the Pro models.

The iPhone Duo is more compromised. Despite its premium price, it has only two 48MP rear cameras and lacks a dedicated telephoto camera, variable aperture, ProRes and Apple Log. Its strengths are instead its fold-specific shooting features and dual-screen flexibility.

The iPhone Air and iPhone 17e are the least versatile, with just a single 48MP rear camera.

Our choice: If photography and video are your priority, buy the iPhone 18 Pro. It offers the same camera system as the Pro Max for less money and in a more manageable size.

Which iPhone has the best battery life? iPhone 18 Pro Max

Apple

The iPhone 18 Pro Max has the best battery life of any current iPhone, with Apple rating it for up to 45 hours of video playback. That puts it comfortably ahead of the smaller iPhone 18 Pro and makes battery life one of the strongest reasons to choose the Pro Max.

The iPhone Duo comes surprisingly close, with up to 44 hours of video playback when using its outer 5.4-inch display. However, battery life drops to around 31 hours when using the larger 7.6-inch folding display, so the Pro Max remains the better choice if endurance is your priority.

The iPhone 18 Pro is also excellent, offering up to 36 hours of video playback. That makes it a good compromise if you want strong battery life without carrying the much larger and heavier Pro Max.

Further down the range, the iPhone 17 offers up to 30 hours, making it the best mainstream option for battery life. The iPhone Air manages around 27 hours despite its exceptionally thin design, while the iPhone 17e reaches 26 hours.

The older iPhone 16 trails the current lineup at up to 22 hours of video playback.

Our choice: If battery life matters above everything else, the iPhone 18 Pro Max is the clear winner. Its combination of a 45-hour rating, huge 6.9-inch display and Pro-level performance makes it particularly well suited to heavy users, travellers and anyone who wants to get through a long day without worrying about charging.

Here’s how the current iPhone lineup compares in terms of battery life

What is the best value iPhone? iPhone 17

Hannah Cowton-Barnes / Foundry

The iPhone 17 offers the best overall value for money in Apple’s current lineup. The iPhone 17e is cheaper, but the extra $200/£200 for the iPhone 17 buys a surprisingly large number of worthwhile upgrades.

You get a larger 6.3-inch 120Hz ProMotion display with Always-On support and Dynamic Island, rather than the 17e’s standard 60Hz 6.1-inch screen. The iPhone 17 also adds a second 48MP Ultra Wide camera, including macro photography, along with a better 18MP Centre Stage front camera.

Battery life is stronger too, at up to 30 hours of video playback, compared with 26 hours on the iPhone 17e. You also get stronger graphics performance and a more premium overall experience, while both phones start with a generous 256GB of storage.

At $899/£899, the iPhone 17 also compares very favourably with the older iPhone 16. For just $100/£100 more, you get double the base storage, ProMotion, a larger and brighter display, improved cameras, the newer A19 chip and significantly better battery life.

If your priority is spending as little as possible, choose the iPhone 17e which delivers excellent performance for $699/£699. Or seek out a refurbished iPhone from the Apple Refurbished Store or another place that sells refurbished iPhones.

Our choice: In terms of the features and hardware you get for every pound or dollar spent, the iPhone 17 is the sweet spot. For most buyers, it delivers the best balance of price, performance, cameras, display quality, battery life and longevity without paying for Pro-level features they may never use. Even better if you can find a iPhone 17 deal, then you are really getting a bargain.

Best iPhone for gaming: iPhone 18 Pro

Foundry

The iPhone 18 Pro is the best iPhone for gaming for most people, thanks to its combination of the A20 Pro chip, seven-core GPU and improved vapor-chamber cooling.

The A20 Pro is Apple’s fastest iPhone processor, but the cooling system is just as important for gaming. Better heat management should help the iPhone 18 Pro maintain high performance for longer during demanding games, rather than slowing down as the phone gets hot. Its 6.3-inch 120Hz ProMotion display also provides smooth animation and responsive gameplay without making the phone excessively large or heavy.

The iPhone 18 Pro Max offers essentially the same gaming performance, but adds a much larger 6.9-inch display and significantly longer battery life. That arguably makes it the best choice for serious mobile gamers who value screen size and endurance, although it is heavier and costs more.

The iPhone Duo also uses the A20 Pro and has an enormous 7.6-inch folding display, which could be fantastic for some games, but its weight, price and unconventional form factor make it a more specialised choice.

Our choice: For most gamers, the iPhone 18 Pro offers the best balance of performance, cooling, display quality and portability. It’s the best choice if you prefer a more pocketable device but still want top-tier gaming power.

Best iPhone for seniors and older users: iPhone 17e

David Price / Foundry

For most older users, the iPhone 17e is probably the best choice, because it combines a relatively simple feature set with modern performance, strong battery life and a lower price than Apple’s flagship models.

Its 6.1-inch OLED display is large enough to make text, icons and controls easy to see without making the phone too bulky, while the A19 chip should keep it feeling fast for years. It also supports Apple Intelligence and starts with 256GB of storage, so there’s plenty of room for photos, apps and videos.

The iPhone 17 is a better option for someone who would benefit from a larger and more advanced display. Its 6.3-inch ProMotion screen, Always-On support and higher brightness can make scrolling, reading and outdoor use more comfortable. It also offers stronger battery life and better cameras, although it costs more.

We don’t recommend the iPhone Air, Pro Max or Duo for older users. The Air sacrifices battery life and camera flexibility for thinness, while the Pro Max and Duo are much heavier and considerably more expensive.

Our choice: iPhone 17e is the perfect choice for most older users.

Best iPhone for kids: iPhone 17e

Ida Blix

The iPhone 17e is the best iPhone for most children. As Apple’s most affordable current-generation model, it offers the best balance of price, performance and longevity, while being easier to justify than a flagship model if it gets lost or damaged.

It uses the same A19 chip as the iPhone 17, albeit with one fewer GPU core, so it’s easily fast enough for games, social media, schoolwork and Apple Intelligence. Battery life is strong, the 6.1-inch OLED display is a sensible size for smaller hands, and the 48MP camera is more than capable for everyday photos, even though it lacks an Ultra Wide lens.

The iPhone 17 is the better choice for older teenagers who care more about photography, video or display quality. It adds a 48MP Ultra Wide camera, a better front camera and a larger 6.3-inch ProMotion display, but costs considerably more.

A hand-me-down iPhone is also worth considering. It’s the cheapest option and better for the environment, provided you erase the phone first, create a Child Account through Family Sharing, and configure Screen Time and parental controls before handing it over. Read: How to set up an iPhone for a child.

Whichever iPhone you choose, those controls matter. In iOS 27, Apple is expanding Screen Time with new category-based Time Allowances, Ask to Browse, more flexible app schedules and improved contact controls. Communication Safety can also detect and blur sensitive, violent or graphic content.

For very young children, an iPad may still be a better first Apple device. By the time they reach 11 or 12 though, an iPhone becomes much more useful for staying in touch.

Our choice: iPhone 17e for most kids; iPhone 17 for older teens who want better cameras and display quality.

Should you buy an older iPhone?

Macwelt

Buying an older iPhone can be a great way to save money, but the key is choosing a model that still has plenty of useful life ahead of it. Apple typically provides around five to seven years of major iOS updates, with security updates often continuing for longer, so a relatively recent iPhone can remain perfectly usable for years.

We wouldn’t recommend simply buying the cheapest iPhone you can find. Very old models may technically run recent versions of iOS, but performance, battery condition and access to newer features can become increasingly compromised. We currently recommend avoiding anything older than the iPhone 15 Pro because even the iPhone 15 doesn’t support Apple Intelligence. You should definitely avoid models such as the iPhone XS and XR that can no longer run the latest iOS releases.

A refurbished recent-generation iPhone can offer particularly good value. You may be able to buy a former Pro model with better cameras and displays for less than a new entry-level iPhone. Buying from a reputable refurbisher is important, however: check the warranty, battery condition, returns policy and whether genuine replacement parts have been used. Apple’s own refurbished iPhones include a new battery and outer shell and come with a one-year warranty.

Our advice: A discounted or refurbished iPhone 16 or newer should offer an excellent combination of price, features and longevity.

entry.title: Apple reportedly slashes employee AI usage limits amid ‘cost-cutting effort’
entry.content:
Macworld

Apple took its time jumping on the AI bandwagon, announcing Apple Intelligence as late as 2024 (nearly three and a half years after the release of DALL-E, and one and a half after ChatGPT) then delaying some of the platform’s flagship features for years after that. But these days the company is a committed proponent of “truly helpful AI that’s centered around you and your needs,” as it writes on the dedicated Apple Intelligence page on its website.

Product pages for the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Duo extol their ability to handle AI workloads, and similar language is used to market the iMac, iPad mini, Apple Watch Series 12, HomeView, and pretty much every other product Apple sells. Former CEO Tim Cook said AI is critical to Apple’s products back in 2023, while new boss John Ternus told Wired last month that the company is “absolutely going to leverage AI” to build incredible products.

However, as much as it encourages customers to enjoy the benefits of AI, Apple has seemingly soured on excessive use of the technology by its own employees. In a new report, Bloomberg claims the company has begun “reducing employee budgets for artificial intelligence usage as part of a cost-cutting effort.”

Citing anonymous people with knowledge of the change, leaker Mark Gurman says Apple last month reduced the daily AI spending cap for some engineers from $300 to $200, and is planning to make further cuts which could see limits drop as low as $100. “Many groups outside of engineering already face a $100 daily cap, but Apple has considered reducing that limit to as little as $25 for some teams,” Gurman adds. Staff who believe these limits will impede their ability to do their job can ask for an exemption.

The spending limits relate to the tokens used by AI providers to track the volume and nature of usage, and to set fees. Complex, data-intensive tasks such as debugging code may cost more tokens than the lighter usage typical among consumers.

Some Apple employees will therefore need to be more conservative in the data-processing demands they place on AI. But others, apparently, won’t need to change anything about their approach. Gurman’s sources claim that “few workers were using their full $300 daily allowances, making the previous limits unnecessarily generous,” which suggests the savings obtained through the measure will be small.

Aside from those public comments praising the usefulness of AI, this is a surprising stance from a company which in its most recent financial disclosure announced its “best fiscal year ever.” But Apple has long been a company obsessed with spotting and eliminating unnecessary costs, with Cook (who came from an operations background) famous for his ability to optimise a supply chain.

Last month’s initial AI spending cut, while it happened on Ternus’s watch, may have been a decision made, or at least floated, while Cook was still in charge. But the plan to cut deeper shows that Ternus is just as keen as his predecessor on running an efficient company.

And after all, as he said in the Wired interview linked above, “We don’t want to ship AI for AI’s sake. When we’re doing it right, people won’t have to think about whether it was AI that made this happen or more traditional software. What matters is, did we build something that they really love?”
